title: The Mouse Deer and the Elephant
summary: An arrogant elephant wants to trample the mouse deer. But the mouse deer has an idea about a tree that is about to fall.
moral: Great strength without thinking is easily fooled. Do not be arrogant, and use your wits well.
pages: In the shady forest, the mouse deer was strolling along, whistling. Suddenly the ground shook: thump, thump, thump! A huge elephant walked toward it.
'Move aside, little mouse deer!' barked the elephant. 'I am the strongest in this forest. Whoever blocks me will be trampled!' The mouse deer trembled, but its mind began to work.
'Wait, mighty elephant!' cried the mouse deer. 'This big tree is leaning and about to fall on the village. I have been holding it up so it will not fall. But my strength is so small...'
The elephant scratched its head. 'Hmm, then let me hold it. My strength must be enough!' It pushed the tree trunk with all its might.
'Great!' said the mouse deer. 'Do not let go, all right? I will go and find a rope to prop it up.' The elephant nodded proudly, while the mouse deer walked away holding back its laughter.
One hour passed. Two hours passed. The mouse deer did not return. The elephant kept pushing, drenched in sweat. 'Mouse deer, where is the rope?' it called weakly.
The sun began to set. The elephant looked at the tree: it had not moved at all. 'This tree was never leaning! I have been tricked!' it growled, but the mouse deer was already far away.
Meanwhile, the mouse deer was enjoying itself by the river. It knew it had survived thanks to its wits. The elephant too learned not to be arrogant. The end.
